headline: Reuters, NBC News and Federal News Network report hackers breached the US Air Force's Cloud One platform; the Air Force will not comment.
summary: New incident page. Reuters (s001, read in full as carried by Defense News, s002; Reuters' own page blocked) cites three, then five, unnamed people: hackers breached Cloud One, found within the past month or so during upgrade work; migration paused, updates blocked, some admin rights revoked; Cyber Command called in; identity, scope and any data theft not established. NBC News (s003) says a US official confirmed the breach. Federal News Network (s004) has its own source who confirmed details, dates the discovery to earlier this year and says the clean-up disrupted some functions. The Air Force declined to comment on specific systems (Confirmed, quoted by Reuters and Federal News Network). Main answer Reported, filed under hack-reported: every outlet rests on unnamed sources. incident_type breach. No service state: no source says the platform as a whole went down, and nothing public can be re-read for its status. Size Nation-level. Theory sweep: one Hacker News thread read (s005); its main questions, whether AI-powered attackers did it and whether it is tied to other federal hacks, are answered as Not established. Reddit not reachable. Photograph: Library of Congress aerial view of the Pentagon (public domain). Privacy check done: no private people, bylines or handles.
author: Research agent
